title: Cosφ equals one, but PF is lower: where the power calculation loses harmonics
description: Why coincidence of the fundamental harmonic phases does not mean equality of kW and kVA: calculation of the true power factor with distorted current.
seo_title: Cosφ equals one, but PF is lower: where the power calculation loses harmonics
seo_description: Why coincidence of the fundamental harmonic phases does not mean equality of kW and kVA: calculation of the true power factor with distorted current.
seo_keywords: Cosφ equals one, but PF is lower where the power calculation loses harmonics
content:
In the power supply report, cosφ = 1 is stated, and on this basis the entire apparent power of the load was equated to active power. For a nonlinear consumer, such a conclusion may be incorrect. Coincidence of the phases of the fundamental harmonics of voltage and current does not eliminate higher harmonic current. The true power factor takes the RMS current as a whole into account, so it can remain noticeably below unity with an ideal phase-shift indicator.

Which two indicators were confused

The displacement factor describes the angle between the fundamental harmonics of voltage and current. At zero angle, its cosine equals one. The true power factor PF is the ratio of active power P to apparent power S. For the single-phase case, S is calculated from the RMS values of voltage and current: S = U × I. If the current waveform is distorted, its RMS value is not limited to the fundamental harmonic.

In the Schneider Electric guide, these indicators are separated. With sinusoidal voltage, active power is related to the fundamental harmonic of current, whereas the RMS current in the denominator includes harmonic components. The customary cosφ entry in a passport or on a screen therefore requires clarifying the meaning of the field, not automatically transferring it into any power calculation.

One complete calculation for a nonlinear load

Let us set an ideal sinusoidal voltage with an RMS value of 230 V. The fundamental harmonic of current has an RMS value of 8 A and is in phase with the voltage. The total RMS value of all higher harmonics of current is 6 A. These components are established for one steady-state mode; interharmonics and the DC component are absent from the model.

The total RMS current equals √(8² + 6²) = 10 A. Adding 8 and 6 arithmetically is not allowed: orthogonal harmonic components give the sum of squares of RMS values. The apparent power is 230 × 10 = 2300 VA, or 2.3 kVA. The fundamental phase indicator indeed remains cosφ₁ = 1.

With the given sinusoidal voltage, active power equals 230 × 8 × 1 = 1840 W. The true PF = 1840 / 2300 = 0.8. A calculator who substituted unity instead of the true coefficient would have obtained 2300 W and overestimated active power by 460 W. At the same time, the RMS current of 10 A is not an instrument error: it includes the actually specified harmonic part.

How to verify the result via current distortion

If the current THD is defined relative to the fundamental harmonic, in our task it equals 6 / 8 = 0.75, or 75 %. For sinusoidal voltage, PF = cosφ₁ / √(1 + THD²). Substitution gives 1 / √(1 + 0.75²) = 0.8. This is an independent expression of the same model, convenient for checking analyser fields.

Percentages are converted to a fraction before squaring. Using 75 instead of 0.75 would lead to a different erroneous result. In addition, some distortion indicators are normalised to the total RMS current. In the example, the ratio 6 / 10 equals 60 %. It cannot be substituted into a formula where normalisation to the fundamental harmonic is explicitly defined. The protocol must preserve both the designation and the definition of the field.

What this calculation changes in the technical decision

It refutes the specific equality of active and apparent power. For selecting power supply, 1.84 kW cannot be considered the sole description of the load while forgetting about 2.3 kVA and the RMS current. For calculating consumed active energy, conversely, watts cannot be substituted with volt-amperes. Data are used for their intended purpose, not replaced by the most convenient number.

The calculation does not automatically show the amount of the penalty imposed by the energy supplier. Commercial metering, intervals and contractual indicators are established separately. Also, cosφ₁ = 1 is not a ground, without calculation, for connecting compensating capacitors. In the example under consideration, the phase shift of the fundamental harmonic is already absent; acting on harmonics requires a different subject assessment.

What records to request instead of a single cosφ photo

Request simultaneous U, I, P and S, as well as the definition of the displayed PF and distortion indicators. Clarify the voltage waveform: if it is significantly distorted, the shortened formula through the fundamental harmonic no longer describes all active power. The relevant model and measurement data must be used, not a convenient assumption of a pure sine wave.

For comparing before and after equipment change, a comparable operating mode is selected. Low no-load current and nominal operation may have different characteristics. A single screenshot does not replace binding to load, time and configuration. The original readings are retained, correcting the conclusion about which power they confirm.

If a project or report equated kW to kVA solely on the basis of cosφ = 1, submit the original fields to NPI "Nedra" via the application form. The question under review is specific: whether the current waveform was taken into account when determining the true power factor. Work on an operating installation and the choice of correction means require an independent technical decision.
